note: Turns: the turn around the 3rd with the metronome, the same turn inside a short run, then the book's falling pentatonic run, which turns round Mi on its way home. The old Stage selector of tempos and Key selector are now moves (any key, 60 to 80 bpm), every tool written at 60; the run is described as the book writes it, and each block has its feel or fix line.

exercise.title: Turns
exercise.why: A turn is the smallest run there is, a note with the neighbour above and the neighbour below, and the runs of soul and R&B are mostly turns joined by steps.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together, at {{=bpm}}. Sing the turn around {{3}}: {{3}}, {{4}}, {{3}}, {{2}}, four notes in one beat, then hold {{3}} for three beats. Sing it on "ah".
Practice until all four notes show as separate steps in your line.
{{?bpm}}At a faster tempo the turn smears into a wobble first, so keep it light.

Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together. Climb {{1}}, {{2}}, {{3}}, sing the turn around {{3}}, then run down {{3}}, {{2}}, {{1}}. Sing the climb on "oo", and open to "ah" on the turn.
Practice until the turn sits inside the run without slowing it.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, but the turn is the same shape around {{3}}.

Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run falls from the high Do through La and Sol to Mi, turns round Mi, and steps down to Do, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it on "ah", and move to "oo" for the high passes.
If a pass smears, listen to it and come in on the next one.
